findings.text: Thread debug state management offers a routine that releases every ptrace breakpoint slot for a given thread and clears its virtual status images, plus a per CPU reload routine that programs the four address registers and the control register from CPU images while loading a reserved value into the status register.

Breakpoint notification handling offers a die chain callback that filters for debug events and delegates to an internal trap dispatcher, plus a perf read hook that currently accepts its argument and returns without effect.

Legacy platform support exposes a helper reporting whether PNP BIOS legacy devices are absent, a global pointer publishing the active clock event device, a cached interrupt mask image, a bitmap of IO APIC routed IRQs, the XT compatible interrupt chip, and the selectable legacy PIC descriptor with its null fallback.

Timer and trap bring up exposes a PIT selection and init pair that either disables the PIT or enables it and publishes it globally, a PIT clocksource init routine, early and full IDT setup routines, and a predicate testing whether an address corresponds to the fixed fault workaround slot.

Clearing ptrace breakpoints iterates over the full hardware breakpoint count, unregisters each slot, stores null back, then zeroes both virtual status images so no stale trap or control bits survive a flush.

Debug register reload always programs address registers in order from first to last, then loads a reserved pattern into the status register before loading the control image, ensuring status is defined before control takes effect.

The trap dispatcher ignores events with no trap bits, otherwise walks every breakpoint register, skips entries whose trap bit is clear or that lack a perf event, defers execute breakpoints when a single step is also pending, clears the handled trap bit in the shared status image, delivers a perf event, and sets the resume flag for execute breakpoints to avoid immediate reentry.

The dispatcher requests further processing only when the current thread virtual image retains trap bits or the incoming status carries non trap causes; otherwise it stops notification, while the early no trap case and non debug notifications complete without action.
DMA resume resets both controller reset ports, then for all eight channels writes a zero base address and a count of one, and finally enables the cascade channel so the low channels remain usable.

DMA syscore registration is refused when the first page port reads all ones, indicating removed legacy DMA, and on recent firmware years when PNP BIOS legacy devices are reported absent; otherwise the resume handler is registered and success is reported.

PIT use is required when the boot CPU lacks a timestamp counter, otherwise it follows an APIC need check; when unused the PIT is stopped under interrupt protection and init reports false, when used the PIT event source is initialized and published globally with true reported.

PIT clocksource registration is skipped on multiprocessor systems, when the high precision timer is active, or when the PIT event source is not periodic; otherwise the PIT clocksource init result is returned.

8259 mask state is tracked in a cached image updated under lock, with bit set meaning masked, and each mask or unmask operation writes the appropriate master or slave cached image to its mask port selected by the IRQ range.

Pending and in service checks select master or slave command ports by IRQ range, the pending test masks the read value with the IRQ bit while the in service test brackets the read between mode select writes that first select the status view and then restore the request view.

Mask and acknowledge first treats a cached masked IRQ as possibly spurious and verifies it against hardware, otherwise it records the mask; real handling masks the device, issues specific end of interrupt sequences to slave then master for high IRQs or to master alone for low IRQs, and spurious cases are logged once per IRQ and counted before being handled as real.

Trigger save preserves only non reserved bits with distinct masks for the two bytes, restore writes both bytes back, suspend only saves, resume reinitializes the controllers with the stored auto mode then restores triggers, and shutdown masks all interrupts without saving.

Controller init records the auto mode, masks the master, issues the init sequence that sets vector bases for master and slave and cascade wiring, selects auto or normal end of interrupt mode, switches the acknowledge handler accordingly, waits briefly for hardware settle, then restores both cached masks.

Probing honors a platform compat flag by skipping hardware access, otherwise it masks the slave, writes a test pattern that excludes the cascade line to the master mask, reads it back, and on mismatch switches the global PIC pointer to the null implementation; both paths return the legacy IRQ count.

Gate construction always marks entries present and uses the kernel code segment; kernel gates use the lowest privilege level while system gates allow user access, default gates use no host stack switch while stack variants select a numbered stack, and task gates encode a descriptor selector.

Early IDT content covers debug and breakpoint plus page fault on 32 bit and virtualization exception on capable guests; the full table adds arithmetic, device, segment, protection, machine check, control protection and virtualization communication vectors with stack switching for selected fault entries, and overflow remains user accessible.

Compatibility system call vector setup depends on build and runtime enablement, selecting an emulation entry when emulation is configured and a 32 bit entry on 32 bit builds, and the full trap setup installs it only when the runtime enable check succeeds.

APIC IDT content is conditional on build options, covering inter processor, thermal, threshold, deferred error, timer, platform, posted interrupt, guest perf, work, spurious, error and posted MSI vectors only when their respective features are enabled.

The IDT storage is page aligned with size derived from entry count and descriptor size, its descriptor length is one less than the table size and initially points at the table, and a later mapping step places the table at a fixed read only entry area address and repoints the descriptor there.

Reassigning an IRQ to the legacy PIC disables the line without waiting, clears its IO APIC routed bit, installs the XT chip with level handling and level status, reenables the line, and invokes the local APIC legacy vector helper.

All cached mask updates and 8259 port sequences for mask, unmask, pending checks, acknowledge, full init, global mask and unmask, and probe test are performed while holding the 8259 spin lock with interrupts saved and restored.
DMA resume claims the DMA lock before touching reset, address, count and cascade controls and releases it afterward, making the whole resume programming appear atomic to other DMA users.
Stopping the PIT when it is not needed is done under an interrupt scoped guard so that the disable sequence cannot race interrupt entry on the local CPU.
DMA and 8259 power management each pair a constant operations table holding resume plus suspend and shutdown for the PIC with a syscore node pointing at that table, registered once during init.

The XT interrupt chip descriptor carries a name and callbacks mapping mask and disable to the same mask helper, unmask to the unmask helper, and masked acknowledge to either the full acknowledge routine or the simple mask helper depending on auto mode.

Legacy PIC indirection uses a table of IRQ count, chip pointer and callbacks for masking and unmasking with global mask and restore plus init and probe and pending testing and IRQ adoption; the null table reports zero IRQs with a dummy chip and no effect callbacks while the default table wires the 8259 helpers and the global pointer starts at the default.

IDT gate specifications carry a vector number, stack selector, gate type, privilege level, handler address and segment, with the builder forcing the present bit set; the IDT itself is an array of hardware descriptors plus a descriptor holding a limit and base address.

Thread debug images include an array of perf breakpoint slots plus virtual status and control images that are cleared on flush and consulted by the trap dispatcher to decide whether user handling is still required.

Breakpoint trap flow moves from status fetch to early completion when no trap bits are set, else per register triage with execute breakpoints yielding to pending single step, then per hit status clear and perf delivery with resume flag for execute faults, ending in stop to suppress further handling or completion when virtual or residual causes need generic debug processing.

8259 power and masking lifecycle moves from probe selection between default and null, to init programming, to runtime mask and unmask updates, with suspend saving trigger mode, shutdown masking all, resume reinitializing then restoring trigger mode, and global mask and restore offering coarse control.

IDT bring up moves from early trap install and descriptor load, to full trap install with optional compatibility vector install gated on runtime enablement, with a separate page fault only table available for early fault handling and a final step that fixes the descriptor to a read only entry area mapping.

PIT selection moves from feature and APIC need evaluation to either a disabled terminal state reporting absence or an enabled state where the event source is initialized and published globally, with clocksource registration further gated on single CPU, absence of high precision timing, and periodic mode.
The debug die notifier is the external entry for breakpoint exceptions, returning completion for unrelated events and otherwise returning the dispatcher verdict for stop versus further processing.
Early and full trap setup routines are boot entries that populate the IDT from constant tables and, for the early stage, load the descriptor so subsequent faults use the new table.
DMA and PIC init routines are boot entries that conditionally register syscore handlers after presence checks, ensuring resume and shutdown callbacks exist only when the hardware is believed present.

A small indirect branch tracking self test provides a code entry deliberately lacking the expected landing marker so that the control protection fault path can be exercised and its handler can signal success through the return register.

Unexpected legacy PIC interrupts can appear even when masked, especially on cascade linked lines, so treating every cached masked event as spurious without an in service check would drop real interrupts; the code mitigates by verifying against hardware, warning once per line, and counting such events.

Leaving the PIT running when unused wastes host CPU time in virtual machines due to pointless masked interrupts, and registering it as a clocksource on multiprocessor systems risks contention on its global lock, so the code stops it when unused and refuses clocksource use beyond one CPU.

Detecting legacy DMA by reading a page port can be confused by firmware reuse of a neighboring port for POST codes and by removed devices returning all ones, and probing an uninitialized PIC can fail expectations, so the code avoids the aliased port and honors a platform compat flag to skip probing.

Deferring execute breakpoints when single step is pending avoids misattributing a fault as a trap and preserves step precedence; clearing the wrong trap bit or omitting the resume flag would cause repeated faults or lost breakpoints.

Keeping the IDT at a discoverable writable address would leak kernel location through the store descriptor instruction and expose the table to arbitrary writes, so the design relocates the descriptor to a fixed read only entry area mapping.
Privilege and stack defaults are zero for kernel privilege, three for user privilege, and zero meaning no stack switch.

Cached mask reset is 0xffff covering sixteen lines, DMA resume covers eight channels with cascade on channel four using address zero and count one, and trigger save preserve masks are 0xF8 for the first byte and 0xDE for the second.

8259 programming uses mask value 0xff, init command 0x11, specific end of interrupt base 0x60, status select codes 0x0B and 0x0A, and a one hundred microsecond settle delay, with vector bases derived from ISA IRQ zero and eight and cascade wiring on IR2.

IDT descriptor limit is table size minus one where table size is entry count times hardware descriptor size, trigger storage holds two bytes, and the legacy fault workaround test checks whether the index of an address within the table equals six.

DMA absence is signaled by a page port read of 0xFF and modern firmware cutoff at year 2017 combined with absent PNP BIOS devices, while PIC probe uses a test pattern with all bits set except the cascade line.
